newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Stock exchange members to mull negotiable fees.
newsitem.headline: Stock exchange members to mull negotiable fees.

text.p: Hong Kong's stock exchange has issued a consultation paper asking members to consider adopting a negotiable commission system or retain the current flat rate system, the exchange said in an announcement on Friday.
"The first choice is to introduce negotiability of brokerage above a certain transaction value -- HK$5 million to HK$7 million have been suggested," it said.

This would meet the government's wish to introduce negotiating flexibility and would reflect the reality that a broker's clients already have the power to negotiate and are using it, the announcement said.
"The second choice is for no change in the present brokerage structure because of fears that this (negotiability) would arouse unwarranted competition among brokers," it said.
The consultation paper points out that evidence from other exchanges suggests the introduction of negotiable brokerage does not necessarily cause a downward spiral in rates, the announcement said.
The paper also points out that failure to introduce negotiability would leave Hong Kong as the only market "regionally and internationally with a flat minimum rate", it said.

"In the Far Eastern markets which are of direct relevance to Hong Kong's competitive position, Taiwan is the only market with a lower minimum brokerage fee. Thailand and China have significantly higher minimums," it said.
All other Asian exchanges, including Japan, Malaysia and Singapore, have sliding rates which start at four or more times the Hong Kong minimum, it added.

"The exchange urged its members to participate in the consultation to enable it to continue negotiating with the government for a reduction in stamp duty as part of an overall reduction in transaction costs," the announcement said.
The exchange issued the consultation paper on Friday and has requested that questionnaires contained in the paper be returned by February 10, a stock exchange official said.
